approach: Direct SAT attack on n=3 R=26 (K=2), seqcounter pseudo-Boolean sum encoding
why_failed: Timeout at 120s and 600s on 2,091,510 clauses / 673,068 vars. Bottleneck is the PB sum encoding (729 equations x 52 literals), not clause count. This is a timeout, NOT UNSAT.

approach: Direct SAT n=3 R=26 with symmetry breaking (K=2, K=3)
why_failed: Still timeout (K=2 at ~700s, K=3 at 400s). Symmetries were not the bottleneck; the PB sum encoding is.

approach: Direct SAT n=3 R=26 with mtotalizer cardinality encoding (27% fewer clauses, 31% fewer vars)
why_failed: Still TIMEOUT at 660s. Better base encoding, worth keeping for future LNS/CEGAR work, but not sufficient alone for direct SAT.

approach: Direct SAT n=3 R=26 with K=7 (adder encoding, vastly larger search space)
why_failed: Timeout. K=7 search space is vastly larger than K=2; direct SAT is the wrong tool here.

approach: LNS repair with k >= 6 triples on the current SAT encoding
why_failed: Timeouts with the current encoding; needs a better encoding first. (Note: LNS with k <= 5 is provably UNSAT -- also do not retry.)

approach: Z3 for the n=3 tensor SAT encoding
why_failed: ~20x slower than bit-blasted SAT on n=2; not competitive for this problem.

approach: Single-triple repair of a broken decomposition (delete one triple, re-solve)
why_failed: Proven impossible in the exhibited case by flattening-rank evidence. Some breakages need coordinated multi-triple moves; single-triple repair is not always sufficient.
